newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel firm, Russian premia ease off.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel firm, Russian premia ease off.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run held firm on Monday but Russian high sulphurs were weaker on perception of better supply, traders said.
The low sulphur market was thinly discussed but one offer level was heard at $110 fob a tonne. While some dismissed this as optimistic others believed it justified by the rise in crude.
Two low sulphur cargoes were believed loading in Europe before mid-June.
Premiums on Russian straight-run were off, with buying interest somewhat diminished and supplies easier as logisitical wrinkles in the inland supply chain get ironed out.
Two M-100s were seen in Tallinn and another two in Klaipeda, with offer levels no higher than two means plus $5, traders said.
